project.type: 2-storey reinforced-concrete villa with MEP on a real plot

phases.purpose: Turn 'I want a house' into a written brief, a first budget and a go / no-go decision before any design money is spent.
inputs: Owner wishes: family size, number of bedrooms, parking, garden, future extension (third floor?)
Plot (owned or candidate), approximate area and location
Money available (own funds, loan), target handover date
Local planning rules for the district (permitted height, setbacks, coverage) - from the district technical office, not guessed

steps.text: Interview the owner and write the design brief (rooms, areas, adjacencies, finish level A/B/C, special needs).
steps.note: O.X report editor + document templates can hold the brief; no brief/room-programme tool.

steps.text: Fix the areas: net room programme, then gross built-up area (BUA) = net / efficiency (0.80-0.85 for a villa incl. walls, stair, void).
steps.note: A spreadsheet does it; no dedicated programme sheet.

steps.text: Check plot rules: setbacks, max coverage %, number of floors, max height, parking count, easements.
steps.note: No zoning / setback checker. Demo can only type the numbers into the project notes.

steps.text: Order-of-magnitude budget = BUA x cost per m2 for the finish level (rule of thumb, from recent local tenders, NOT a design figure); add design fees, permit fees, utilities connection, contingency 10-15 %.
steps.note: dc_tnd prices a BOQ (overhead, profit, contingency, VAT); dc_fs does NPV/IRR/payback. Neither ships a cost-per-m2 benchmark.

steps.text: Feasibility if it is an investment (sell/rent): NPV, IRR, payback, sensitivity. Skip for an owner-occupied house.
steps.note: Inputs are the owner's own numbers.

steps.text: Risk list at idea stage (soil unknown, permit delay, price escalation, owner changes) with a first mitigation each.
steps.note: Risk register + Monte Carlo schedule risk.

steps.text: Choose delivery route: design-bid-build with separate consultant and contractor (recommended for a house), or design-build, or owner-managed with labour-only crews.
steps.note: Decision; affects phase 7.

steps.text: Go / no-go and sign the brief; open the project file and the document register.
steps.note: tpChooser creates the project; setup stores name/client/number/currency. Template house2 is the R.X starter (see data inventory).

outputs: Project number and folder / register opened
checks: Brief signed by owner (date on it)
Budget >= low estimate x 1.1 or scope reduced
BUA within plot rules (coverage x floors)
Every wish has either a room, a budget line or a written 'not now'
rules: RULE OF THUMB: villa BUA ~ 1.2-1.4 x net living area.
RULE OF THUMB: contingency 10 % at brief stage, 5 % at tender, 3-5 % at construction.
RULE OF THUMB: soft costs (design, supervision, permits, utilities) 8-15 % of construction cost.
mistakes: Starting design before the plot rules are known
Budget without utilities connection, landscaping, boundary wall, furniture
Forgetting the owner's future extension (column and footing sizes then change)
phases.demo: Fast: ch1 'project' already does the template + setup. Add a 20-second 'brief' caption and a dc_fs sample; do not spend long here.

phases.title_en: Site: survey, soil, boundary, utilities, access
phases.title_ar: الموقع: الرفع المساحي والتربة والحدود والمرافق والوصول
phases.purpose: Know the ground (levels, boundary, soil, water table) and what the plot connects to, before the structure and the drainage are designed.
inputs: Plot title / cadastral sheet (حيازة / عقد / كروكي)
Neighbours' building heights and foundation levels (adjacent excavation risk)

steps.text: Locate the plot on the map, record coordinates (WGS84 and the local grid), north direction, nearby roads.
steps.note: G.X map + converter + 'Set project location'. Imagery needs internet.

steps.text: Order a topographic survey: total station / GNSS, grid of spot levels (every 5-10 m on a small plot + all break lines), boundary pegs, neighbours' walls, road kerb levels, manhole/pole positions.
steps.note: Field work. T.O X receives the result.

steps.text: Import survey points (PNEZD/CSV), build TIN surface, contours (0.25-0.5 m for a plot), spot-check against raw points.

ids.label: survey_10 [SURVEY Home > Create Ground Data > Create TIN surface]

steps.note: S.X (Civil 3D-like): points, TIN, contours, volumes, traverse with Bowditch (mod_cxsx), LandXML import/export.

steps.text: Draw the boundary as a closed polyline from the survey; compute area and compare with the title area (difference tolerance per authority).
steps.note: CAD polyline + area. No 'compare with title' check.

steps.text: Soil investigation: 2-3 boreholes (or 1 per ~150-200 m2) to 6-10 m or to firm layer; SPT every 1-1.5 m; sampling; water table; lab tests (grain size, Atterberg, unit weight, shear strength / consolidation, chemical tests: sulphates, chlorides, pH). Geotechnical report with recommended foundation type, allowable bearing, settlement, aggressive-soil advice.
steps.note: Field + lab. Egyptian reference: ECP 202 (soil mechanics and foundations; check edition/clauses).

steps.text: Enter the borehole log and compute a preliminary bearing capacity (Terzaghi) as a screening check of the geotechnical report.
steps.note: dcBearing = Terzaghi qu with shape factors, FS. No settlement, no layered soil, no ECP 202 method.

steps.text: Seismic and wind site data: seismic zone / design ground acceleration from the code map, site class from the boreholes, basic wind speed; liquefaction screening if loose saturated sand.
steps.note: Eurocode-8-form spectrum (the form ECP 201 uses) and ASCE 7 base shear; wind panel says ECP 201 has its own chapter and does NOT apply it. Zone values must be typed from the code map.

steps.text: Sun path and orientation study for the building mass and glazing (shade, summer sun).
steps.note: Sun path, shadows on the model, energy.

steps.text: Utilities survey: electricity (nearest transformer / LV pole, available kVA), water (main DN, pressure), sewer (invert level of the nearest manhole - decides gravity vs septic), gas, telecom, storm. Written statement from each utility.

ids.label: survey_17 [SURVEY Home > Create Design > Pipe Network]

steps.note: Can draw/import the lines as layers; S.X pipe catalogue exists (placeholder sizes). No utility-capacity check.

steps.text: Access and logistics: road width for concrete trucks/pump, crane or no crane, material storage, neighbours, working hours.
steps.note: No site-logistics tool; draw on the C.X plan.

steps.text: Earthworks estimate: existing vs finished ground levels, cut/fill volume, disposal; excavation volume of foundations later (phase 6).
steps.note: F.X reality capture: TIN, cut and fill; S.X volumes.

steps.text: Site report: summary of constraints and design implications (soil, level, utilities, orientation).
steps.note: Report templates incl. technical and site visit.

outputs: Topographic drawing (DWG/PDF) with boundary, levels, contours
Soil report with allowable bearing and foundation advice
checks: Survey closes: control points tie within tolerance (typical total-station traverse closure 1:10 000, per spec)
Boundary area vs title within the authority's tolerance
Soil report signed by a geotechnical consultant / accredited lab; borehole depth >= 1.5 x footing width below founding level (rule of thumb) or reaches firm layer
Water table known; aggressive soil classified (sulphate / chloride)
Every utility has a written connection point
rules: RULE OF THUMB: 1 borehole per 150-200 m2 of footprint, minimum 2; depth 6-10 m for a 2-storey house on normal soil.
RULE OF THUMB: allowable bearing of 100-200 kPa is common for Egyptian normal soils; weak clays / fill / high water table are common exceptions - the soil report decides, not this figure.
RULE OF THUMB: spot levels every 5-10 m on a small plot; contour interval 0.25-0.5 m.
mistakes: Designing foundations without a soil report
Taking levels from the road only (plot is lower than the street -> flooding, and sewer cannot be gravity)
Ignoring neighbour's foundation depth (needs shoring or underpinning)
Using a wrong datum between survey and drawings
phases.duration: 2-4 weeks (survey 3-5 days, boreholes + lab 1-3 weeks, report 1 week)
phases.demo: Today ch2 'site' only does survey/excavation/cost on the sample site. Add: borehole log typed into dc_soil -> bearing result; env_eq inputs typed; utilities shown as GIS layers.

phases.title_ar: التصميم المعماري: الفكرة ثم المخطط ثم الواجهات والقطاعات
phases.purpose: Turn the brief and plot into a buildable plan: layout, facades, sections, openings - the geometry the structure and MEP will follow.

steps.text: Mass and site plan: footprint inside setbacks, parking, entrance, garden, orientation (living towards north/breeze, minimum west glass).

ids.label: model_146 [MODEL Massing & Site > Model Site > Toposurface]

steps.note: Site plan view in R.X is station-specific data; massing tools partly present.

steps.text: Concept plans by hand or CAD: bubble diagram -> block plan with room areas.
steps.note: H.X home plan: drag rooms; C.X blocks library (arch 28, elec 19, plumb 9, fire 8, HVAC 13).

steps.text: Set levels and grids in R.X. Ground floor level +0.00 = chosen vs road kerb (usually +0.45 to +1.0 m above road, per local rule); floor-to-floor 3.0-3.2 m; parapet 1.0 m.
steps.note: Template house2 has levels Ground 0 / First 3 / Roof 6 and 4 grids.

steps.text: Draw external and internal walls (structure grid first, then 25 cm external / 12 cm internal masonry, per Egyptian practice), doors, windows, columns positions coincide with grid.
steps.note: R.X walls/doors/windows (hosted openings). 45 family types + 12 layered assemblies; assembly sets wall thickness only, 3D stays a single box. NOTE: template house2 has 16 walls, 0 columns, 0 beams (see gaps).

steps.text: Floors, stair (riser 15-17 cm, tread 28-30 cm, width >= 1.0 m; headroom >= 2.2 m), roof (flat with parapet and slope 1-2 % to drains), rooms with area tags.
steps.note: All present as R.X tools.

steps.text: Check areas and clearances: room areas, net/gross, stair geometry, door widths (0.9 m main, 0.8 m rooms, 0.7 m bath), window sills.
steps.note: Room area tags and Area (Gross/Rentable).

steps.text: Elevations (4), sections (2, through stair and wet areas), plan with dims.
steps.note: SVG, no WebGL; 'to CAD' puts them on layers for PDF/DXF.

steps.text: Interior layout and finishes: materials, furniture, lights.
steps.note: H.X materials (floors 19, walls 9, ...) and furniture models.

steps.text: Render and walkthrough images for the owner approval.
steps.note: Render Studio (stills up to 8K, turntable video) and true-vector SVG export of the view.

steps.text: Owner review round(s) and freeze; issue 'architectural design freeze' drawing set (plans, elevations, sections, door/window schedule).
steps.note: Sheet composer exists; door/window schedule via R.X schedule (rv_sched). No design-freeze status workflow.

steps.text: Submit for the building permit (authority forms: architectural + structural + soil report + title). Egypt: unified building law (Law 119 of 2008 and its executive regulations - verify current text).
steps.note: Outside the software; tracked in the register (dc_new / dc_reg).

outputs: Architectural drawing set (site plan, plans, 4 elevations, 2 sections, schedules)
R.X model Level of Development ~ LOD 200-300 (walls, openings, floors, stair, roof)
checks: Plan inside setbacks and coverage limits
Stair rise/tread comply, headroom >= 2.2 m
Every room has window/ventilation (or mechanical vent) and every wet area stacks over wet area where possible
Grid spacing realistic for RC (spans 3.5-5.5 m, avoid > 6 m without extra beam)
Owner signature on the freeze set
rules: RULE OF THUMB: keep slab spans <= 5 m for economical solid slab+beam; align walls above walls; stack wet rooms.
RULE OF THUMB: floor-to-floor 3.0-3.2 m; clear height 2.7-2.9 m after finishes.
RULE OF THUMB: external masonry 25 cm, internal 12 cm; wall self-weight ~ 2.0-3.5 kN/m2 of wall face - the load figure comes from ECP 201 / the materials, not from this.
mistakes: Drawing walls first and columns later (columns end up in the middle of doors)
Wet areas not stacked -> long drains
No room for ducts / shafts (MEP riser 40x60 cm each)
Stair with wrong rise/tread because floor height changed
phases.demo: Current ch1 'rx' + ch2 start. Needed: explicit grid + level first, then perimeter walls (thickness 0.25), then columns on the grid, then openings; sections after. The template house2 has no columns: demo must place them or the template must be extended.

phases.title_en: Structural system choice, loads and preliminary sizing
phases.purpose: Pick the frame system and foundation type, define the loads, and size members roughly so the architect and MEP can reserve space.
inputs: Soil report (allowable bearing, depth, water table)
Codes chosen: ECP 201 loads, ECP 203 concrete, ECP 202 foundations (or Eurocode 1/2/7, or ACI 318 + ASCE 7)

steps.text: Choose the system: RC skeleton (columns + beams + solid slab) = default for a villa; flat slab / hollow-block (ribbed) alternatives; masonry fill, not load-bearing.
steps.note: Engineering decision.

steps.text: Choose the foundation type from the soil report and column loads: isolated footings + tie beams (default on good soil), strap/combined footings near boundary, raft if footings cover > ~40-50 % of the footprint or soil is weak/water high, piles only if the report requires.
steps.note: Engineering decision; revisit after load take-down.

steps.text: Fix materials: concrete grade (Egypt uses cube strength fcu: typical C25-C30 for a villa frame; check ECP 203 exposure and durability for foundations in sulphate soil), reinforcing steel grade (common Egyptian grades 24/35 mild, 36/52 high-yield, 40/60 high-strength - verify with the supplier and ES standard), cover, cement type (sulphate-resisting where the soil report says so).
steps.note: p_codes lists the codes (titles only, clause numbers deliberately not reproduced). No material-grade table.

steps.text: Define loads per ECP 201 (check clauses): dead (self weight + finishes + partitions), live by occupancy (residential rooms ~2 kN/m2, balconies/stairs higher - from the code table), roof live/maintenance, wind, seismic zone, earth pressure, water. Typical finishes allowance ~1.5-2.0 kN/m2 on floors; masonry wall line loads.

ids.label: model_55 [MODEL Structure > Analytical Model > Load Combinations]

steps.note: R.X Load Combinations (floor loads, EN 1990 6.10 / ASCE 7 / characteristic) exists but no ECP 201 table and no wall line loads.

steps.text: Load combinations: ECP 203 ultimate (typical 1.4 D + 1.6 L, plus wind/seismic combinations - check the clause) and service combination for deflection/cracking/bearing.

ids.label: model_55 [MODEL Structure > Analytical Model > Load Combinations]

steps.note: EN/ASCE/characteristic forms only.

steps.text: Preliminary sizing by span/depth: slab t >= span/30-35 (one-way) or span/35-40 (two-way continuous); beam depth span/10-12 (simply supported to continuous), width 20-30 cm; column from load: Ac ~ N / (0.35-0.45 x fcu) as first guess; footing area = service load / allowable bearing x 1.1.
steps.note: Rules of thumb only; no pre-sizing tool. Demo can type them into the R.X Properties (rv_props).

steps.text: Layout the structure on the grid: column positions (also at stair corners, around shafts), beam lines under walls, slab panels, cantilevers/balconies, expansion/construction joints, lift pit if any.
steps.note: R.X elements exist; no automatic framing from walls.

steps.text: Check column load take-down (tributary area x total load x floors) and footing area once; revise sizes; fix final grid and dimensions with the architect.
steps.note: No load take-down tool. p_calc sheets 'bear' (bearing pressure under base) can check one footing.

steps.text: Coordination meeting: structure vs architecture vs MEP (beam depth under ducts, column vs door, slab openings for shafts).
steps.note: N.X clash + MOM tool.

steps.text: Write the structural design basis (1-2 pages): codes, loads, materials, foundation type, assumptions, software/method.
steps.note: Report editor; no design-basis template.

outputs: Structural layout drawings (column grid + beam layout + slab panels + foundation type) - preliminary
Updated R.X model with columns/beams/slabs/foundations at preliminary sizes
checks: Column continuity from foundation to roof (no column ends on a beam unless designed)
Total preliminary concrete within the rule-of-thumb range (see phase 6)
Footing areas fit inside the plot and clear neighbours
All spans <= limits used in the span/depth table
Design basis signed by the engineer in charge
rules: RULE OF THUMB: total concrete in a villa skeleton ~ 0.30-0.40 m3 per m2 of BUA incl. foundations; reinforcing steel 90-130 kg per m3 of concrete (~ 35-50 kg/m2 BUA). A quantity far outside this range = recheck.

RULE OF THUMB: villa column grid 4-5.5 m, columns 25x60 to 30x70 cm in Egyptian practice (long side along the wall), beams 25x60 cm typical; footing 1.2-2.2 m square for 400-900 kN service load on 150 kPa soil.
RULE OF THUMB: the 1st trial footing area = service load x 1.1 / allowable bearing.
mistakes: Choosing isolated footings when they almost touch -> should be a raft
Forgetting the tie beams / grade beams and the ground slab
Using live loads from habit instead of the code table
Changing the architectural plan after the structure is fixed
phases.demo: Highlight: place columns on the grid, beams on the wall lines, foundation pads under columns, show the 'load take-down' table (needs a small build - see gaps).

phases.title_ar: التحليل والتصميم الإنشائي التفصيلي (بلاطات وكمرات وأعمدة وأساسات وسلالم وحوائط ساندة)
phases.purpose: Design every structural element to the code, detail the reinforcement and issue drawings, schedules and a calculation report that a checker can follow.
inputs: Phase 3 design basis, layout, loads, materials
MEP penetrations and equipment weights (water tank, AC units, lift)

steps.text: Build the analysis model or the hand-calc scheme: slab panels (support conditions per edge), continuous beams, frames (2D or 3D), foundation model. State assumptions (rigid/elastic supports, cracked section factors).

ids.label: model_54 [MODEL Structure > Analytical Model > Boundary Conditions]

steps.note: R.X can tag boundary conditions (fixed/pinned/roller/free) on columns/foundations but there is NO structural solver (no frame/beam/slab analysis).

steps.text: Slabs: solid slab one-way (long/short >= 2) or two-way; bending moments from code coefficient tables or yield-line/FE; check minimum thickness for deflection; min steel (shrinkage/temperature) and max spacing; cantilevers/balconies design incl. edge beam torsion; shear check (usually no stirrups).
steps.note: Only the strip/beam flexure+shear sheet `flex` (ACI 318 form, simplified, cylinder f'c). No moment coefficients, no two-way slab, no deflection.

steps.text: Beams: flexure (rectangular / T-beam, singly then doubly reinforced), shear + stirrup spacing, torsion for edge/spandrel beams, deflection (span/depth or computed), crack width, support moment at continuity, development of top steel into columns.
steps.note: `flex` gives As, As,min, tension-controlled strain, phi*Mn, phi*Vc only. No stirrup design, no T-beam, no torsion/deflection/crack.

steps.text: Columns: axial + uniaxial/biaxial moment (interaction diagram), slenderness (braced/unbraced), minimum eccentricity, steel ratio limits (min ~0.8 %, max ~4-6 % - check ECP 203), tie spacing/size, splice zone.
steps.note: No column design sheet or interaction diagram.

steps.text: Foundations: service-load bearing check (q <= allowable, no uplift under combinations), settlement/differential settlement, ultimate design: one-way shear, punching shear at d/2, flexure in both directions, development length of bars, tie beams/strap design; raft: soil springs or rigid method, punching under columns, edge details. Egyptian reference ECP 202 (check clauses).
steps.note: `bear` = W/A vs qa for one base; Terzaghi qu from the log. No punching, no one-way shear for footings, no raft, no settlement.

steps.text: Stairs: waist slab as one-way inclined slab (span horizontal projection), landings, loads (self weight of steps + finishes + live), reinforcement incl. bent bars at re-entrant corners, support on beams/walls.
steps.note: Can run `flex` per metre strip; stair geometry is in R.X.

steps.text: Retaining walls / basement walls / ramp walls if the plot has level change: active/at-rest earth pressure + surcharge + water; stability (overturning FS >= ~1.5-2.0, sliding FS >= ~1.5, bearing); stem and base design; drainage and waterproofing.
steps.note: Only flotation (`float`, for a well) exists - no retaining wall sheet.

steps.text: Seismic: ECP 201 zone + site class -> base shear, distribution, drift; check frame detailing class (ductility). Wind on a 2-storey villa rarely governs.
steps.note: Eurocode-8-form spectrum and ASCE 7 base shear (ECP 201's own spectrum/zone table not coded; wind: ECP 201 has its own chapter - the panel says it does not apply it).

steps.text: Serviceability: deflection limit (e.g. span/250 total, span/350-500 after partitions - check ECP 203), crack width (typical 0.3 mm external/0.4 mm internal - check exposure class), vibration for long spans.
steps.note: Not computed anywhere.

steps.text: Detailing: cover, bar spacing, development length ld and lap length (rule of thumb ld ~ 40-50 db for high-yield bars in 25-30 MPa cube concrete, lap = 1.3 ld for ~50 % splice - COMPUTE with the ECP 203 / ACI formula), hooks and bends, stirrup closure at 135 deg, splice location (columns just above slab, beams away from supports), stirrup spacing near supports (confinement zone), curtailment points.
steps.note: Ribbon entries Cover/Area/Path/Fabric Sheet/Couplers are stubs; Rebar entry runs the lift-station rebar viewer (`rb`/`p_rebar`) only.

steps.text: Reinforcement schedules / bar bending schedule (BBS): mark, diameter, shape code, cut length, number, total length, weight (kg = d2/162 x m, d in mm). Totals per element and per diameter for ordering.
steps.note: dc_rb = rebar take-off tab of document control; `rb` = station rebar. Not generated from R.X columns/beams/slabs.

steps.text: Structural drawings: foundation plan + sections, column schedule, beam layout + elevations, slab reinforcement plans per floor, stair detail, general notes (grades, cover, laps, curing), title block.
steps.note: C.X drawing + sheet composer + title blocks A1-A4. Drawings must be drawn; none auto-produced from a design.

steps.text: Calculation report: inputs, load table, results, pass/fail per check, reference clause. Independent check by a second engineer (+ authority stamp).
steps.note: p_review recomputes the calc sheets and compares with the model; wf_struct is an ordered review (model data > calcs > soil > rebar > seismic > wind > liquefaction > clashes > drawing set).

outputs: Structural drawings: foundation, columns, beams, slabs, stair, details
Structural quantities (concrete m3, steel kg, formwork m2)
checks: Flexure: Mu <= phi*Mn at every critical section; As >= As,min; As <= As,max (tension-controlled / ductile)
Shear: Vu <= phi*Vn; stirrup spacing <= code max; minimum shear steel where required
Punching (footings, flat slabs): vu <= phi*vc at d/2 from the column face
Deflection: computed or span/depth ratio satisfied; crack width <= limit for the exposure class
Columns: Pu-Mu point inside the interaction diagram; slenderness checked; 0.8 % <= rho <= code max (check ECP 203)
Footing: service q <= allowable (and >= 0 everywhere, i.e. no uplift); differential settlement <= typical L/500 (check the code)
Detailing: cover >= code/exposure; ld and lap provided >= required; bar spacing between min and max
Overall: quantities per m2 BUA in the rule-of-thumb band; two-engineer sign-off
rules: ECP 203 works with cube strength fcu and gamma_c = 1.5, gamma_s = 1.15 (check the clauses); ACI 318 works with cylinder f'c (rough conversion f'c ~ 0.8 fcu, NEVER use for final design); Eurocode 2 uses fck cylinder. T.O X `flex` is ACI/SBC-style - say so on screen.
RULE OF THUMB steel weight per m3 concrete: footings 60-100, slabs 70-100, beams 130-180, columns 150-250 kg; average 100-130 kg/m3.
RULE OF THUMB min dims: column >= 25x25 cm (check), slab >= 12 cm (roof/floor), beam width >= 20-25 cm, cover 25-30 mm in beams/columns indoors, 50-75 mm against soil.
RULE OF THUMB two-way slab: effective depth d ~ L/35-L/40; simply supported one-way: L/20-L/25 (d); the code table is the authority.
mistakes: Designing with unconfirmed loads or an unchecked soil bearing
Missing top steel at continuous supports and cantilevers
Stirrups too wide at column/beam joints, 90-degree stirrup hooks
Forgetting punching at footing and slab-column joints
Laps all at the same section
Cover too small against soil -> corrosion
Copying ACI formulas for an ECP submission
phases.duration: 3-6 weeks for a villa (design) + 1 week checks
phases.demo: Demo can truthfully show: R.X sizes -> concrete quantities -> `flex` bending check of one slab strip and one beam -> `bear` check of one footing -> rebar weight from dc_rb. It must say 'screening, ACI-form'. Anything more (columns, punching, deflection, ECP 203) is a BUILD item, see gaps 1-3.

phases.title_ar: تصميم الكهروميكانيكا: الكهرباء والتكييف والسباكة والصرف والتيار الخفيف
phases.purpose: Design the building services so they fit the architecture and structure, are safe, and can be quantified and priced.
inputs: Architectural plans (rooms, areas, use, glazing, orientation)
Structural layout (beam depths, shafts, slab openings)
Utility connection letters (kVA, water pressure, sewer level)
Owner requirements (AC type, solar heater, smart home, CCTV)

steps.text: ELECTRICAL - Load schedule: every room's lighting (W/m2 or lux method), sockets (typ. 10 A / 16 A), AC units, water heaters, kitchen, pumps, lift, EV charger; connected load, demand/diversity factors, total kVA, phase balance (single/three-phase supply).

ids.label: model_134 [MODEL Analyze > Reports & Schedules > Panel Schedules]

steps.note: R.X placements carry watts; Panel Schedules assign loads to the nearest panel and sum connected watts. No demand/diversity factors, no kVA/phase-balance report.

steps.text: Distribution: main distribution board (MDB), sub-boards per floor, circuits (lighting 10 A, sockets 16 A, AC dedicated), RCDs 30 mA on socket/wet circuits, metering point from the utility.

ids.label: model_134 [MODEL Analyze > Reports & Schedules > Panel Schedules]

steps.note: Panel schedule only; no single-line diagram tool.

steps.text: Cable and breaker sizing: design current Ib = P/(sqrt3 x V x pf) (3-ph) or P/(V x pf) (1-ph); breaker In >= Ib; cable Iz >= In from the code's ampacity table with derating (grouping, temperature, installation); voltage drop <= ~3 % lighting / 5 % total (check local rule); short-circuit check at the board.
steps.note: AC unit table: power from cooling and COP, current, breaker from the standard rating series, cable from voltage drop (resistance at conductor temperature). Ampacity tables are NOT typed in: user pastes them. Motor/transformer/voltage-drop calc in env_qc. No lighting/socket circuit sizing, no short-circuit calc.

steps.text: Earthing and protection: TN-C-S or TT per utility, earth electrode (rod/plate/foundation earth - often the footing steel is bonded), main equipotential bonding, lightning protection if required, surge protection at MDB.
steps.note: wf_mep has a step 'Earthing, lightning, fire, ventilation' that only checks a list; no earthing resistance calc.

steps.text: Lighting design: lux target per room (rule of thumb living 100-150, kitchen/desk 300, corridors 100, bath 150-200), lumen method N = E x A / (F x UF x MF), fixture schedule, switching.
steps.note: No lighting calculation tool.

steps.text: HVAC - cooling load room by room (envelope U-values, glass by orientation, people, lights, equipment, ventilation, infiltration), diversity, select unit capacity (split HP / TR) with margin 10 %.

ids.label: model_128 [MODEL Analyze > Energy Analysis > Heating and Cooling Loads]

steps.note: V.X hourly design-day estimate (conduction with sol-air, Meinel solar, people, lights, vent, infiltration; no thermal storage = conservative). All inputs editable placeholders.

steps.text: Select equipment: split / ducted split / VRF, indoor units per room, outdoor units on roof/balcony with service clearance, refrigerant pipe length limits, condensate drains.
steps.note: Equipment library (AHU, FCU, split, VRF, chillers, diffusers) is placeholder data.

steps.text: Duct sizing (if ducted): flow per diffuser, equal-friction method, velocity limits, aspect ratio, fittings K values entered by the user, critical-path pressure, fan static.
steps.note: Darcy-Weisbach + Swamee-Jain, Huebscher rectangular equivalent; duct plan assigns flows downstream and finds the critical path. No fitting tables (user enters K).

steps.text: Fresh air and extract: toilets/kitchen extract (typ. 10-15 ACH bath, kitchen hood), stairwell/garage rules.
steps.note: No ventilation calc.

steps.text: PLUMBING - Water supply: fixture units per fixture, demand (probable flow from fixture units), pipe sizes by velocity (<= 1.5-2.0 m/s) and pressure loss (Hazen-Williams), pressure at highest fixture (>= 1-1.5 bar), ground tank + pump or roof tank (volume = persons x 150-250 L/day x 1-2 days), booster pump selection.

ids.label: model_80 [MODEL Systems > Plumbing & Piping > Plumbing Fixture]

steps.note: Hazen-Williams head loss + velocity and pump/motor calc exist. No fixture-unit demand table, no tank-volume or pipe-sizing tool, R.X Pipe/Pipe Sizing are stubs.

steps.text: Hot water: solar heater + electric backup, pipe lengths, insulation.

Drainage and vent: fixture units to branch/stack sizes (typ. WC 100 mm, others 50-75 mm), slopes (1-2 %: >= 1:50 for 100 mm, 1:100 for >= 150 mm), vents, manhole at turns/ends (spacing <= 15-25 m), inspection chambers, grease trap for kitchen if required.
steps.note: Manning full-flow capacity of a gravity pipe; S.X pipe/structure catalogue (placeholder); T.X pipe runs with DN/spec/BOM/iso (not linked to R.X).

steps.text: Sewer or septic: connect to public sewer if invert level allows gravity (check cover and slope), otherwise septic tank + soakaway/cesspit (بيارة) sized by persons x 150-200 L/day x retention 1-2 days; setback from water well / boundary per authority.
steps.note: No septic/soakaway tool. Networks sample data (sewer/storm/water/fire) exist from the lift-station sample only.

steps.text: Rainwater: roof drains (area x rainfall intensity), downpipes, storm connection or soakaway.
Fire fighting: extinguishers per area, civil-defence approval for the building class, hose reel/standpipe if required by class; smoke detectors.
steps.note: C.X fire symbols (8); network sample for fire mains exists in sample data.

steps.text: LOW-CURRENT - Data/telephone: structured cabling (Cat6) to each room, rack location, wifi AP positions; TV/satellite; intercom/video door phone; CCTV cameras + NVR (storage = cameras x bitrate x days); fire alarm panel + detectors/sounders + battery sizing; access control; smart-home bus if any.
steps.note: Only CAD symbols in the block library; no riser diagram, no cable schedule, no battery/NVR calc.

steps.text: Draw MEP layouts: lighting+socket plans, panel schedule, AC layout + duct, water + drainage plans/risers/isometrics, low-current plans, schedules, specifications.
steps.note: CAD + sheets; T.X iso sheet generator for pipes.

steps.text: MEP check: wf_mep runs pump, motor, voltage drop, transformer, pipe velocity, safety, earthing in order and says 'missing' where no data.
steps.note: Checks station-type items (pump/transformer) well; building items are mostly missing.

outputs: Electrical: load schedule, single-line diagram, panel schedules, cable/breaker table, lighting plan, socket plan, earthing detail
HVAC: cooling-load table, unit schedule, duct drawing + table, drain plan
Plumbing: fixture-unit table, supply/drain/vent plans, risers, tank & pump data, septic/sewer detail
checks: Electrical: Ib <= In <= Iz for every circuit; VD <= limit; earth fault loop / RCD operation; main kVA <= utility approval; every socket circuit RCD-protected
HVAC: unit capacity >= room load x (1.0-1.15); duct velocity <= limit; total static within fan data; condensate falls
Plumbing: velocity within 0.6-2.0 m/s; residual pressure >= 1 bar at worst fixture; drain slope >= minimum and flow depth < ~0.7 D; vent for every trap
Septic/sewer: capacity >= persons x per-capita; levels allow gravity
Fire: civil-defence approval in file
All penetrations through slabs and beams are shown on the structural set
rules: RULE OF THUMB HVAC (Egypt, residential): 120-180 W per m2 conditioned area; 1 TR = 3.517 kW; 1 HP split ~ 9000-12000 Btu/h; ~1 HP per 10-14 m2 in a villa room with average glazing. Load calc supersedes this.
RULE OF THUMB electrical: villa connected load 80-150 W/m2, after diversity ~ 40-70 W/m2; typical main supply 3-phase 380/220 V 50 Hz, 63-125 A for a villa (utility decides).
RULE OF THUMB water: 150-250 L/person/day (check local), tank volume 1-2 days; supply pipe velocity 1.0-1.5 m/s.
RULE OF THUMB drains: 100 mm at 1 % (1:100) minimum for WC branches where allowed (check code), 50 mm basin/shower at 2 %; manholes every <= 15-20 m.
RULE OF THUMB duct: main 6-8 m/s, branches 3-5 m/s, friction 0.8-1.0 Pa/m (residential 0.6-0.8).
mistakes: AC outdoor units without airflow clearance
Condensate drains forgotten
Sockets without RCD in bathrooms/kitchens
Panel placed in bathroom/kitchen wall or behind a door
Septic tank too close to a water well or boundary
No riser shafts reserved -> pipes through beams
Cable sized for current only (no voltage drop / derating)
phases.duration: 3-6 weeks for all disciplines (parallel to structural design)
phases.demo: Good existing coverage for HVAC cooling load > duct > AC electrical. Electrical load schedule/panel and plumbing sizing need small builds to be convincing (gaps 5-7).

phases.title_en: Coordination, quantities, BOQ, specifications and cost estimate
phases.title_ar: التنسيق وحصر الكميات والمقايسة والمواصفات والتكلفة
phases.purpose: Prove the design is clash-free, then extract every quantity, attach specifications and prices, and produce the engineer's estimate that the tender and the budget rely on.

steps.note: N.X clash detective + coordination checks (specs vs codes) + BCF-shaped issues (viewpoint, section cut, snapshot). Needs MEP as 3D geometry to be meaningful: R.X Duct/Pipe are stubs; only boxes (Mechanical Equipment, Device, Plumbing Fixture...).

steps.text: Check headroom/clear height under beams, slab openings vs shafts, door clearances, equipment access.
steps.note: Section planes and measure tools; no rule-based headroom check.

steps.text: Quantity take-off by trade, per phase of work (excavation, blinding, concrete by element and grade, formwork area, steel kg, masonry m2/m3 minus openings, plaster, flooring, ceilings, doors/windows, paint, waterproofing, MEP points/lengths).

Each BOQ item points to a spec section.

Engineer's estimate with cost per m2

Quantities sanity vs rules of thumb: concrete 0.30-0.40 m3/m2 BUA, steel 100-130 kg/m3, blockwork area ~ 1.0-1.5 m2 per m2 BUA, plaster area ~ 2.0-2.8 m2 per m2 BUA (RULES OF THUMB)
No BOQ line with qty 0 or rate 0 (wf_qa reports it)
Every BOQ item has unit, spec reference and source of rate
Estimate within +/-10 % of independent cost-per-m2 benchmark

RULE OF THUMB: add waste: concrete 3-5 %, steel 3-5 % (laps/cut), tiles 7-10 %, brick 3-5 %.

No allowance for laps/waste/formwork
Rates without date and source
Spec says one thing, BOQ item another
Forgetting preliminaries (site office, water/electricity for works, scaffolding)

steps.note: O.X has 11 letter/form templates (letter, RFI, IR, MIR, MOM, transmittal, NCR, daily report, payment certificate, variation order, checklist) - no tender/contract template.

steps.note: Register + CDE states + follow-up dashboard.

Bid comparison: price per trade vs estimate, unbalanced rates, qualifications, schedule, references, payment terms; normalise to the same scope.

Contract signing: contract sum, program, key staff, insurance, performance bond, advance payment guarantee; start-work order.

steps.note: Interim payment certificate (cumulative, retention, advance recovery), MOM, issue tracker, calendar.

checks: Bids on identical scope and BOQ
Contract sum = BOQ total + agreed adjustments
Bonds/insurance received before start
Retention and advance recovery terms written in the IPC settings

RULE OF THUMB: reject a bid > 15 % below the estimate without a written explanation (unbalanced / missing scope)

No variation procedure
Vague drawings -> endless extra claims
Starting work without permit and insurance

phases.title_en: Planning: WBS, schedule, resources, cash flow, safety plan
phases.title_ar: التخطيط: هيكل الأعمال والجدول والموارد والتدفق النقدي وخطة السلامة

inputs: Crew productivities (local), calendar (Friday off, Ramadan, holidays)

steps.note: P.X WBS + activity template library (4 templates, 62 activities, placeholder durations).

steps.text: Add logic: FS links, lags (concrete cure 7 days before stripping soffit formwork - spec; masonry after frame; MEP first fix before plaster; second fix after plaster), constraints, milestones.
steps.note: CPM, critical path, float, baseline, drag bars (gantt).

Safety plan (HSE): hazards by activity (excavation collapse, falls from height, formwork failure, electrocution, lifting), PPE, edge protection, scaffolding inspection, emergency plan, permits to work; induction.

checks: Critical path is continuous and driven by logical links (no constraints forcing dates)
Float on non-critical branches reported
Calendars include weekends/holidays/curing
Cash flow peak <= available funds + financing
Every high-risk activity has a method statement
rules: RULE OF THUMB villa durations (BUA ~ 400 m2): site setup 1 wk; excavation + blinding 1-2 wks; foundations 3-4 wks; each floor frame (columns, beams, slab) 3-4 wks; masonry 4-6 wks (overlaps with 2nd floor); MEP first fix 4-6 wks; plaster 4-6 wks; second fix + finishes 12-18 wks; external works 4-6 wks; testing/handover 2-3 wks; total 10-14 months.

RULE OF THUMB productivity (per crew/day): concrete pour 40-60 m3 with a pump; formwork 12-18 m2/carpenter-day; steel fixing 250-400 kg/steel-fixer-day; blockwork (25 cm) 8-12 m2/mason-day; plaster 20-30 m2/plasterer-day; tiling 8-15 m2/tiler-day. Replace with the contractor's real data.

No curing/strip time between pours
Plaster before MEP first fix
Ignoring Ramadan/holiday productivity
Cash flow ignoring retention and payment delays

phases.title_en: Construction in true order, with inspections and hold points
phases.title_ar: التنفيذ بالترتيب الصحيح مع الفحوصات ونقاط الإيقاف
phases.purpose: Build the house in the only order that works, and prove quality at each stage before the next one covers it.
inputs: Method statements and ITPs (inspection and test plans)

steps.text: Hoarding/fence, site office, store, toilets, temporary water and power (distribution board with RCD), signboard, safety signs, neighbours' condition photos.
Surveyor sets out grid lines and benchmark; offsets kept outside excavation; verify against plot boundary.

stages.crews: Site engineer, surveyor + chainman, foreman, 2-4 labourers, security
stages.equip: Total station/level, string line, hand tools, water tank
stages.hold: HOLD: set-out checked by the consultant before excavation. Record: set-out sheet.
stages.tox: P: o_sheet, lb_ox (daily report/checklist), rc_open (stakeout points CSV) ; no set-out tool

steps.text: Strip topsoil; excavate to founding level (leave last 10-20 cm for hand finish); side slopes or shoring near neighbours/roads; dewatering if the water table is above the base; keep spoil away from the edge.
Check level, dimensions, soil type against the report; geotechnical engineer confirms bearing stratum (plate test or proof by inspection).

stages.crews: Excavator operator, truck drivers, 4-6 labourers, safety officer
stages.equip: Excavator, loader, tipper trucks, dewatering pump, shoring/trench boxes
stages.hold: HOLD: founding level and soil acceptance (consultant + geotech). Record: excavation approval form with level readings.
stages.tox: P: rc_qty (volume), env_gr (dewatering estimate), dc_soil; no excavation-inspection form

steps.text: Compact base; lay polyethylene sheet if specified; pour lean concrete 5-10 cm (C10-C15) to level; anti-termite treatment of soil where specified; apply bituminous/membrane protection to footing and tie-beam sides below ground if specified.

stages.equip: Mixer or ready-mix truck, vibrator, level
stages.hold: HOLD: blinding level and dimensions; waterproofing continuity. Record: blinding approval.
stages.tox: P: lb_ox checklist; no spec/ITP library

stages.t: Footings, neck columns and tie beams

steps.text: Mark footing positions on blinding; fix bottom mat reinforcement with cover blocks (spacers 50-75 mm); column starter bars with correct lap length and tie position; formwork for neck columns/tie beams; pour footing, then columns to underside of tie beam, then beams (or per design).
Backfill in 20-30 cm layers, compact (typ. >= 95 % modified Proctor - per spec) after concrete reaches strength.

stages.crews: Steel fixers 4-6, carpenters 3-4, concrete gang 6-8, foreman, QC engineer
stages.equip: Rebar cutter/bender, vibrator, concrete pump or crane bucket, ready-mix trucks, compaction roller/plate
stages.hold: HOLD 1: rebar inspection before pour (diameter, spacing, cover, laps, starters, cleanliness, formwork). HOLD 2: pour with approved mix, slump test, cubes. Records: rebar inspection request (IR), pour record, cube register.
stages.tox: P: lb_ox (IR, MIR, checklist) + dc_reg + rq follow-up; no cube/slump statistics tool

stages.t: Ground slab / plinth beams and DPC

steps.text: Sub-base fill + compaction, PE sheet, reinforcement mesh/bars, services sleeves cast in (drains, conduits), pour slab on grade or suspended ground slab; plinth DPC (horizontal damp-proof course) under first masonry course; termite barrier.

stages.hold: HOLD: sleeves/embedded services inspected BEFORE pour (MEP + QC). Record: embedded works checklist.
stages.tox: P: nv_clash + R.X Plumbing Fixture/Device boxes (for sleeve positions); no sleeve schedule

stages.t: Columns, beams and slabs - each floor

steps.text: Cycle per floor: column reinforcement + formwork -> pour columns; beam and slab formwork + props (shores) -> beam/slab reinforcement incl. top steel, stirrups, openings, edge beams -> MEP sleeves and conduits embedded -> inspection -> pour slab and beams monolithically (continuous, 'cold joint' avoided) -> curing >= 7 days (wet burlap / curing compound) -> strip side forms 1-2 days, soffits and props by strength/time per spec (typ. >= 14-21 days for spans, re-propping) -> repeat for next floor; stair cast with the slab.
Level and plumb checks on columns; deflection and cracks watched after strip.

stages.crews: Steel fixers 8-10, carpenters 8-12, concrete gang 8-10, electricians/plumbers (sleeves), foreman, QC
stages.equip: Concrete pump, ready-mix trucks, poker vibrators, props + scaffolding, hoist/crane, rebar bender, level, plumb bob
stages.hold: HOLD 1: formwork and props inspection. HOLD 2: rebar inspection (incl. top steel, stirrups, cover, laps, openings). HOLD 3: MEP embedded works. HOLD 4: pour permit with mix design, slump, temperature, cubes (set of 3 per pour / per 50 m3 or as spec; test 7 and 28 days), curing record. HOLD 5: strip permit.
stages.tox: P: lb_ox, dc_reg, mom_open, is_open, ct_cal; P.X activity chain (p6, xf_p6); no cube-test record/strength acceptance tool

stages.t: Roof slab, parapet, roof waterproofing and tanks
stages.ar: سقف الدور الأخير والبرابيت وعزل الأسطح

steps.text: Slab as 9.6 + parapet, drains, slope screed (1-2 %), thermal insulation, waterproofing membrane with upturns, protection screed and tiles, water tank supports, AC outdoor platforms, flood test (24-48 h) before protection.

stages.equip: Torch/roller, level, water for flood test
stages.hold: HOLD: flood test pass (no leaks after 24-48 h). Record: flood test report.
stages.tox: P: lb_ox checklist; no ITP library

steps.text: Set out walls from grids; first course on DPC; courses with mortar joints 10-12 mm; lintels over openings; tie to columns; chases for conduits/pipes cut after masonry (not through columns); stop 2-3 cm below beam soffit and fill later; control joints; wet bricks before laying.

stages.hold: HOLD: opening sizes, verticality, lintels, chase depth. Record: masonry inspection.
stages.tox: Y: R.X walls drive quantities; P: rv_dim, rv_sched

steps.text: Electrical: conduits and back boxes in walls/ceilings, pulling wire after plaster rough; earth electrode and bonding; panel boxes. Plumbing: water supply pipes (PPR) in chases, drain stacks/branches with correct slope, vent pipes, floor drains, pressure test. HVAC: refrigerant copper lines and condensate drains in walls/ceilings, duct frames; Low-current: conduits for data/CCTV/TV/fire alarm. Fire: pipe/detector conduits.

stages.crews: Electricians 4-6, plumbers 3-5, HVAC fitters 3-4, low-current techs 2
stages.equip: Pipe benders, press tools, pressure-test pump, megger
stages.hold: HOLD: pressure test water pipes (typ. 1.5 x working pressure, 2-24 h per spec), drain water/air test, conduit continuity and earth continuity BEFORE plaster. Records: test certificates.
stages.tox: P: ace_*, du_*, nv_clash; no test-certificate register

steps.text: Prepare surface (clean, wet, mesh over junction of masonry and concrete), 3 coats typical (rough, second, finish) with screeds as guides, corners, cement-sand ratio per spec, curing; external work in shade/curing; check flatness and plumb (typ. 3-5 mm in 2 m).

stages.hold: HOLD: MEP first fix tested and closed before plaster. Record: plaster inspection.
stages.tox: P: BOQ items; no inspection form

stages.t: Floors, wall finishes, ceilings, doors/windows, paint
stages.ar: الأرضيات وتشطيبات الحوائط والأسقف والأبواب والدهانات

steps.text: Screed under floor finishes -> waterproofing in wet rooms + flood test -> wall/floor tiling -> false ceilings/gypsum -> door frames/aluminium windows (often earlier, before plaster) -> joinery -> paint primer + putty + 2 coats -> kitchen units, sanitary ware.

stages.crews: Tilers 6-10, gypsum 3-5, carpenters, aluminium fitters, painters 6-10
stages.hold: HOLD: wet-area waterproofing flood test; tile sampling approval; colour approvals.
stages.tox: P: hx_mat (materials), hx_fur, lb_rx families; no finishes schedule per room

steps.text: Wires pulled, sockets/switches/fixtures, panels terminated and labelled; sanitary fixtures and taps; AC indoor/outdoor units installed, refrigerant vacuum and charge; low-current devices, CCTV cameras, intercom, fire alarm devices.

stages.crews: Electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, low-current techs
stages.hold: HOLD: insulation resistance (megger), earth resistance, RCD trip test, polarity before energising.

steps.text: Boundary wall, gate, paving, drainage connections to sewer/septic, manholes, landscaping, external lighting, gas/water/electric meters rooms, final site clean.

stages.hold: HOLD: manholes and drainage test, sewer connection approved.
stages.tox: P: rc_open/ S.X for levels; S.X pipe lib

steps.text: Run construction as stages 9.1-9.13 (below), each with its inspection request, pass/fail and photo.
steps.note: Documents + register + Telegram photo logger + collection tool exist; hold points are not linked to activities.

steps.text: Track progress: weekly/daily report, percent complete by activity, 4D comparison planned vs actual.
Material approvals: samples, test certificates (steel mill certificate + tensile/bend tests, cement, aggregate sieve, bricks, tiles), delivery notes; MIR (material inspection request).
steps.note: MIR template exists.

steps.text: Variations and claims: variation order, time extension, daily records.
steps.note: Variation order template; IPC.

steps.text: Payment: monthly IPC with progress, retention, advance recovery.
Non-conformance: NCR with root cause, corrective action, closure.
steps.note: NCR template + issues.

outputs: Inspection requests and approvals (set-out, excavation, rebar, pour, embedded, tests)
checks: Concrete: cube compressive strength acceptance per ECP 203 / spec - typical rule: average of consecutive results >= fcu + margin and no single result below a lower limit (CHECK the clause; do not quote numbers without it)
Slump within spec (typical pumpable 100-150 mm, +/-25 mm); no water added on site; temperature limits; pour continuity (no cold joint within initial set time)
Rebar: diameter, spacing +/- tolerance, cover (spacer blocks), laps/hooks, steel certificates; no oil/loose rust
Formwork: dimensions +/- 5-10 mm, plumb, props braced, camber on long spans if spec
Curing >= 7 days; strike times respected
Pressure/leak tests documented BEFORE concealment
As-built deviations recorded for the as-built set
rules: RULE OF THUMB cube sampling: 1 set (3 cubes) per pour per day or per 50 m3 (spec decides); test 7 days (about 65-70 % of 28-day strength expected) and 28 days.
RULE OF THUMB cover blocks: footings 50-75 mm, slabs/beams/columns 20-30 mm (spec decides).
RULE OF THUMB strike: vertical forms 24-48 h, slab soffits 7-14 days with props kept, long spans 21-28 days (spec decides).
RULE OF THUMB crews for a villa: ~25-40 workers at peak (structure phase 20-30, finishing phase 40-60).
mistakes: Pouring without rebar inspection
Adding water to concrete on site
Short curing in Egyptian summer heat (cracks)
Cutting columns/beams for pipes after concrete
Plastering before pressure test
No cube samples kept -> no proof of strength
Removing props early
phases.duration: 10-14 months total (see durations rules in phase 8)
phases.demo: Highest 'show' value: 4D animation by stage plus a single hold-point example (rebar inspection IR -> pass -> pour). Needs a small hold-point/inspection register tool tied to P.X activities (gap 9).

phases.title_en: Testing, commissioning, snagging, handover, as-built, O&M and close-out
phases.title_ar: الاختبارات والتشغيل التجريبي والملاحظات والتسليم والرسومات التنفيذية وكتيبات التشغيل والإغلاق
phases.purpose: Prove the building works, fix what does not, hand over complete records and close the contract.

uncertain: Standards: ECP 203 (concrete), ECP 201 (loads), ECP 202 (soil/foundations) are named from memory of their titles. NO clause number, load value, safety factor or limit is quoted as code text; where the document mentions typical values (gamma_c 1.5, gamma_s 1.15, 1.4 D + 1.6 L, cover, deflection and crack limits, min column size) they are the well-known textbook / Egyptian-practice values marked 'check the clause' - verify against the licensed edition (2018 for ECP 203 is expected, confirm).

Egyptian steel grades (24/35, 36/52, 40/60), cube strength convention (fcu), local standards (ES numbers), Law 119 of 2008 and its regulations, civil-defence and utility rules: stated from general knowledge of Egyptian practice; the editions and current numbers were not looked up (no network research was done for this task).

Every RULE OF THUMB figure (kg steel per m3, W/m2 loads, productivities, durations, cost shares, septic per-capita, velocity ranges) is an order-of-magnitude planning aid from general engineering practice, not from a cited source and not for design.

T.O X state was read from the built page `vx_wired.html` (scratchpad, 2026-11-21 09:12) plus the c_*.js sources; the demo session may have changed chunks since. The registry dump counts 1608 commands (1462 non-stub). Stub flags are runtime values, not guesses. What a 'built' command does in detail was taken from the module notes (rvx.md, qx.md, p2tog.md, mod_cxsx.md, px2.md, lb.md, hxassets.md) and code headers; I did NOT click through each of the ~1400 working commands. Statements like 'no ... tool' mean: nothing found by registry, XDESC and grep for the topic - a quick re-grep is advisable before building.
Libraries (`lib:*`) load their items lazily; the counts (45 R.X types, 12 assemblies, 91 CAD blocks...) are from lb.md, not from the live registry.
